patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Reproduced bug BEFORE fix: run_tests.py passed (weak suite) but report dump showed 6 lines with 101/102 duplicated and cross-customer attribution, total 290. 2) Applied fix (match by unique customer id). 3) AFTER fix: run_tests.py passed; report 4 correct lines, total 165; added assertions 'OK: no duplicate order lines; every line shown to its true owner'; distinct Zenith orders 103/104 retained. 4) git diff shows exactly one changed file matching the patch.
cause: orders_for_customer matched by the non-unique name field; two customers share 'Acme', so every Acme order was attributed to both, producing phantom statement lines and per-customer duplicate emissions in the company-wide report (total inflated 165->290). Fix matches strictly on order['customer_id'] == customer['id'].
